The first two episodes of "The Man" are now available on Apple TV, and this British comedy series has received overwhelmingly positive reviews. Check out the trailer below.

The Man is now streaming on Apple TV

My colleague Ryan earlier reported on the rave reviews "The Man" has been receiving. The show, a British comedy, had its international distribution rights picked up by Apple TV earlier this year.

This is unprecedented for Apple TV, as the streaming platform has never before acquired an English-language series that had already aired on another platform.

"The Man" premiered earlier this year on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two in the UK, and Apple subsequently acquired its international distribution rights in August.

Apple TV subscribers worldwide (excluding the UK) can now watch it, with the UK Apple TV launch expected in 2027.

"The Man" was created, written and directed by Mackenzie Crook ("Detectorists"), who also stars in the show. The cast also includes Pearce Quigley ("The Outlaws"), Lauren Patel ("The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry"), Sir Michael Palin (Monty Python), Sophie Willan ("Ludwig"), Jon Pointing ("Big Boys") and Paul Kaye ("Game of Thrones").

After the first two episodes, new episodes will be released every Wednesday until 4 November.

Below is the official synopsis of "The Man" provided by Apple TV:

"The Man" tells the funny story of the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Since his beloved Clea went missing seven years ago, he has been living a very ordinary life — working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping that Clea will one day return. One day, Brian shares with him an ancient recipe that calls for rainwater, horse manure, and a few alchemical ingredients. Armed with the recipe, Michael sets about creating "homunculi" — magical sprites that can predict the future — with a hint of scepticism, hoping they might answer the question weighing on his mind: "Will I ever see Clea again?" Michael gets help from Kacey (Lauren Patel), a young colleague. Though they could not be more different, the two bond over a shared dislike of their branch manager Gordon (Mackenzie Crook). Their friendship only deepens the frustration and curiosity of their nosy neighbours (Sophie Willan, Jon Pointing), who are desperate to figure out what is going on inside the garden shed.
